description:

Does this pose a risk when charging? Is it necessary to replace the connector?

additional_info.subject: RE: 00439565 - ID0420527-DC/Si-D/FR-[Null]connector issue CRM:02681000101 [ thread::mWWznPgwIrm0dibhR7sG5Bg:: ]
additional_info.body:
Hi Thibaut,
Thank you for raising this concern to us.
Regarding the bladed of pins, the pins must have some sort of “spring movement”, so to allow the CCS Plug, hence the pins, to move and fit into EV sockets. A certain degree of movement is therefore required.
Before proceeding with further assessment or replacement, it is necessary to:
Assess if the movement of the blades is sort of a spring movement, or if the blades are loose/overlapping.
Verify if hotspots or welding is present on the blades.
Verify if this investigation was purely a visual observation on the plugs, or if charging interruptions, TempSensorErrors, or toggling of Pilotstate were detected.
We have checked the last 2 months logs regarding the Cable Temperature sensor errors and found just 6 error flags raised, with no implausible temperature values observed.
If possible, could you please check the above points, or alternatively, we can inform our service team to visit the site for further investigation.
Additionally, if there have been any recent interruptions in charging sessions due to unexpected changes in the pilot state or cable temperature issues, we suggest putting the affected outlet as unavailable and informing us, so we can escalate the issue to our service team for high-priority investigation.
@
recharge.us@siemens.com, this case if from France region regarding SiCharge-D. You can close the ticket 00439565 from your end, we will continue to keep it open on our side for follow-up. Please note, from next communication onward, we will remove ‘recharge.us@siemens.com’ from the email distribution list.
Thank you
Best Regards,
Vishal Dhiman
eMobility Support Team
